Un-chain and aggregate chain-linked volume measures

Source: R/chain_unchain.R
chain_unchain.Rd

Indirect seasonal adjustment of chain-linked Laspeyres-type series (ESS Guidelines on Seasonal Adjustment, item 5.6): the seasonally adjusted components are un-chained, aggregated, and the aggregate is chain-linked again. chain_unchain() un-chains chain volume measures and chain_aggregate() derives the chain volume measure of the aggregate of components, whatever they are (seasonally adjusted components, for instance).

Usage

chain_unchain(
  x,
  cp,
  method = c("ao", "oqo"),
  base_year = NULL,
  pi = NULL,
  overlap_prices = c("year_prices", "current_prices")
)

chain_aggregate(
  x,
  cp,
  method = c("ao", "oqo"),
  base_year = NULL,
  output = c("index", "measure", "both"),
  pi = NULL,
  cp_total = NULL,
  overlap_prices = c("year_prices", "current_prices")
)

Arguments

x

Chain volume measures (in monetary terms) of the components (ts or mts), as returned by chain_link() or chain_laspeyres() with output = "measure", or their seasonally adjusted version.

cp

Current prices of the components (same number of variables as x). It must cover the reference year.

method

Chain-linking technique of x: "ao" or "oqo".

base_year

Reference year of the chain measures. By default, the year before the start of x (or the first year of cp, if later).

pi

Price indices of the components over the previous year (previous year average = 100), needed for method = "oqo" with overlap_prices = "year_prices".

overlap_prices

Only for method = "oqo": prices used to value the overlap period, "year_prices" (default) or "current_prices"; it must be the one used to compute x (see chain_laspeyres()).

output

(chain_aggregate() only) Chain index (the default), chain volume measure or both (see chain_link()).

cp_total

(chain_aggregate() only) Current prices of the aggregate. By default, the sum of cp.

Value

chain_unchain(): a ts (or mts) with the structure of x: the volume of each period at the (average) prices of the previous year, in monetary terms. chain_aggregate(): a ts (see chain_link() for output = "both").

Details

To derive the seasonally adjusted aggregate of seasonally adjusted chain-linked components:

  1. seasonally adjust the chain volume measures of the components (outside the package);

  2. un-chain the seasonally adjusted components: chain_unchain() returns the volume at the prices of the previous year, which is additive within each year (the sum of the components is the volume of the aggregate at the prices of the previous year);

  3. aggregate them and chain-link the aggregate (again with the same technique);

  4. re-reference it to the reference year.

With \(x_t\) the chain volume measure of a component, \(b\) the reference year, \(f\) the frequency and \(\Lambda_y\) the chain level of year \(y\) (see chain_link()), the volume at the prices of the previous year is $$x^{py}_t = \frac{x_t}{cp_b / f} \times \frac{o_{y(t)-1}}{\Lambda_{y(t)-1}},$$ where \(o_y\) is the value of the reference of year \(y\): the annual current prices divided by \(f\) (annual overlap) or the value of the overlap period (one-quarter overlap). The volume index of the aggregate is then \(100 \sum_i x^{py}_{i,t} / \sum_i o_{i,y(t)-1}\), chain-linked with chain_link().

chain_aggregate() does the steps 2 to 4. The reference year of the result is base_year and its annual current prices are those of cp, so that the seasonally adjusted aggregate is normalised to the unadjusted data of the reference year. The annual links are those of the series that are chained or un-chained: chain_unchain() is the exact inverse of chain_link() with output = "measure", and chain_aggregate() applied to the unadjusted chain volume measures of the components gives the chain volume measure of their total (chain_laspeyres()).

The annual totals of the seasonally adjusted data are not forced to be equal to the annual totals of the unadjusted data (an option of the guidelines when users require it and the unadjusted data are additive). This approach only concerns Laspeyres-type series: for other chain-linked indices, only the direct approach is feasible.

With the one-quarter overlap technique, the overlap period is valued at the average prices of the year (see cp_pi2cy()), hence the price indices pi, or at its own current prices (overlap_prices = "current_prices", pi is then not needed). The un-chaining of the first year after the reference year (or of the first year of x if the reference year is not before it) needs the level of the previous year: if the reference year is inside the series, the first year is NA.

References

International Monetary Fund (2018), Quarterly National Accounts Manual (2017 Edition), chapter 8 "Price and Volume Measures", Washington, DC. doi:10.5089/9781475589870.069 .

Eurostat (2015), ESS Guidelines on Seasonal Adjustment (2015 Edition), Luxembourg, Publications Office of the European Union. doi:10.2785/317290 .

See also

chain_link(), chain_laspeyres()

Examples

x <- chain_laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi, base_year = 2010, output = "measure")
# Volumes at the prices of the previous year (additive within each year)
chain_unchain(x[, c("A", "B")], imf_cp, base_year = 2010)
#>                A        B
#> 2011 Q1 156.5686 221.1111
#> 2011 Q2 159.2195 218.0612
#> 2011 Q3 162.5243 214.8980
#> 2011 Q4 164.7573 213.8384
#> 2012 Q1 169.9512 210.4124
#> 2012 Q2 176.8627 203.4343
#> 2012 Q3 187.0297 195.2284
#> 2012 Q4 212.3153 173.4343
#> 2013 Q1 223.5821 166.0000
#> 2013 Q2 236.9849 154.7525
#> 2013 Q3 245.3535 146.3054
#> 2013 Q4 249.1371 141.9608
# Aggregate of the components: the chain volume measure of the total
chain_aggregate(x[, c("A", "B")], imf_cp, base_year = 2010, output = "measure")
#>          Qtr1     Qtr2     Qtr3     Qtr4
#> 2011 377.6797 377.2807 377.4222 378.5957
#> 2012 379.3789 379.3126 381.2686 384.7510
#> 2013 388.6164 390.7664 390.6881 390.1284
